subject: Biotechnology
title: Vectors: DNA Delivery Vehicles
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Vectors: DNA Delivery Vehicles.

hook.text: A gene floating loose in a cell gets destroyed — it needs a vehicle to survive. Enter the vector.

buildup.text: Plasmids are the simplest vectors — small circular DNA molecules that bacteria replicate automatically.

discovery.text: Viral vectors hijack the cell's own machinery — adenoviruses and lentiviruses deliver genes with high efficiency.

twist.text: BACs and YACs carry huge DNA inserts — up to a million base pairs, needed for entire gene complexes.

climax.text: Choosing the right vector determines success — size limits, host range, and safety all matter.

punchline.text: The gene is the passenger — the vector is the ride.

quiz.question: What is a vector in genetic engineering?
options: A chemical that dissolves cell membranes for DNA entry
A DNA molecule that carries foreign genes into cells and ensures their replication
A machine that physically injects DNA into cell nuclei

details.summary: Vectors are DNA molecules used to carry foreign genes into host cells, including plasmids for bacterial cloning, viral vectors for gene therapy, and artificial chromosomes for large DNA segments. Each vector type offers different insert capacities, host ranges, and expression characteristics.
details.whyItMatters: Vectors are genetic engineering's delivery system. The choice of vector determines insert size, expression level, cell type compatibility, and safety profile.
takeaways: Plasmid vectors carry genes into bacteria for cloning and protein production
Viral vectors like AAV and lentivirus deliver therapeutic genes to human cells
Vector design determines insert capacity, expression level, and safety profile

faq.question: What are the main types of vectors used in genetic engineering?
faq.answer: Plasmids carry up to about 15 kilobases into bacteria. Cosmids and BACs handle 40 to 300 kilobases. For human cells, adeno-associated virus carries under 5 kilobases safely, lentivirus carries about 8 kilobases with integration, and adenovirus carries up to 35 kilobases without integration.

faq.question: Why is AAV the most popular gene therapy vector?
faq.answer: AAV rarely integrates into the host genome, reducing cancer risk. It infects many cell types including non-dividing cells. Different AAV serotypes target specific tissues like liver, muscle, or neurons. It causes minimal immune response. Multiple approved gene therapies use AAV vectors successfully.
